name: Neutralization of Hydrochloric Acid with Sodium Hydroxide
explanation: Hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide in a 1:1 mole ratio to yield aqueous sodium chloride and water. The strong acid (H+) and strong base (OH-) neutralize to form H2O, raising pH to 7 and releasing heat.

verification.notes: Classic strong acid-strong base neutralization reaction.

name: Neutralization of Sulfuric Acid with Sodium Hydroxide
explanation: Diprotic sulfuric acid requires two equivalents of sodium hydroxide to reach neutralization, producing soluble sodium sulfate and releasing significant hydration heat.

sources: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics

name: Neutralization of Nitric Acid with Potassium Hydroxide
explanation: Nitric acid neutralizes potassium hydroxide to form potassium nitrate salt solution and water.

name: Neutralization of Acetic Acid with Sodium Hydroxide
explanation: Weak acid acetic acid reacts with strong base NaOH, resulting in a slightly basic equivalence point (pH ~ 8.8) due to sodium acetate hydrolysis.

verification.notes: Weak acid - strong base titration curve.

name: Reaction of Hydrochloric Acid and Sodium Bicarbonate
explanation: Hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium bicarbonate to form carbonic acid, which rapidly decomposes into water and vigorous carbon dioxide gas effervescence.

verification.notes: Classic fizzy acid-carbonate gas evolution reaction.

name: Reaction of Vinegar and Baking Soda
explanation: Baking soda and vinegar react to produce foam and bubbles of carbon dioxide gas while dropping solution temperature slightly.

name: Reaction of Hydrochloric Acid and Calcium Carbonate (Marble)
explanation: Solid marble chips (CaCO3) dissolve in hydrochloric acid with brisk bubbling as CO2 gas is released.

name: Reaction of Hydrochloric Acid and Zinc Metal
explanation: Zinc metal dissolves in hydrochloric acid, displacing hydrogen to evolve flammable hydrogen gas bubbles.

verification.notes: Classic lab preparation of H2 gas.

name: Reaction of Hydrochloric Acid and Magnesium Ribbon
explanation: Magnesium reacts vigorously with hydrochloric acid, releasing rapid hydrogen gas bubbles and significant thermal energy.

name: Reaction of Sulfuric Acid and Iron Filings
explanation: Iron metal dissolves in dilute sulfuric acid, releasing hydrogen gas and forming a pale green iron(II) sulfate solution.

name: Precipitation of Silver Chloride from Silver Nitrate and Sodium Chloride
explanation: Mixing clear silver nitrate and sodium chloride solutions instantly produces a dense white curtain of curdy silver chloride precipitate.

name: Precipitation of Barium Sulfate from Barium Chloride and Sulfuric Acid
explanation: Barium ions react with sulfate ions to form an extremely insoluble fine white precipitate of barium sulfate.

verification.notes: Standard qualitative test for sulfate ions.

name: Precipitation of Barium Sulfate from Barium Chloride and Sodium Sulfate
explanation: Double displacement exchange produces white insoluble barium sulfate solid dispersed in aqueous sodium chloride.

name: Precipitation of Copper(II) Hydroxide
explanation: Adding sodium hydroxide to blue copper sulfate forms a gelatinous light-blue precipitate of copper(II) hydroxide.

name: Precipitation of Iron(III) Hydroxide
explanation: Ferric chloride solution reacts with sodium hydroxide to yield a dark reddish-brown rusty precipitate of iron(III) hydroxide.

name: Displacement of Copper by Zinc Metal
explanation: Zinc metal displaces copper from copper sulfate solution. The blue color fades as zinc sulfate forms and reddish-brown copper metal deposits onto the zinc surface.

name: Displacement of Copper by Iron Filings
explanation: Iron displaces copper from copper sulfate solution, turning the blue solution pale green (FeSO4) while coating iron with metallic copper.

name: Catalyzed Decomposition of Hydrogen Peroxide by Potassium Iodide
explanation: Potassium iodide acts as a homogeneous catalyst, rapidly breaking down hydrogen peroxide into water and warm oxygen gas foam (elephant toothpaste).

name: Catalyzed Decomposition of Hydrogen Peroxide by Manganese(IV) Oxide
explanation: Heterogeneous catalyst manganese dioxide rapidly speeds up H2O2 decomposition to evolve copious oxygen gas.

verification.notes: Standard laboratory method for generating O2 gas.

name: Combustion of Magnesium Metal in Oxygen
explanation: Magnesium burns in oxygen with a dazzling, blinding white light flame, forming a fine white ash of magnesium oxide.

name: Combustion of Hydrogen Gas (Pop Test)
explanation: Hydrogen gas ignites with oxygen with a characteristic squeaky 'pop' sound, combining rapidly to form water vapor droplets.

name: Combustion of Ethanol Fuel
explanation: Ethanol burns smoothly in excess oxygen with a clean blue flame to form carbon dioxide gas and water vapor.

name: Combustion of Sulfur in Oxygen
explanation: Yellow sulfur powder melts and burns with an eerie bright blue flame in oxygen, releasing pungent sulfur dioxide fumes.

name: Phenolphthalein Color Change in Basic Solution
explanation: Phenolphthalein undergoes structural deprotonation above pH 8.2, turning solutions from clear/colorless to brilliant magenta pink.

name: Phenolphthalein Color Reset in Acidic Solution
explanation: Protonation in acidic environment (pH < 8.2) restores the colorless neutral phenolphthalein form.

name: Methyl Orange Color Change in Acidic Solution
explanation: Methyl orange turns red at pH levels below 3.1 upon protonation.

name: Universal Indicator in Strong Acid
explanation: Universal indicator turns deep red in strongly acidic solution (pH 1-2).

name: Universal Indicator in Strong Base
explanation: Universal indicator turns purple / violet in strongly basic solution (pH 12-14).

name: Limewater Test for Carbon Dioxide Gas
explanation: Bubbling CO2 gas through clear limewater produces fine suspended calcium carbonate precipitate, making solution milky white.

verification.notes: Diagnostic limewater test for carbon dioxide gas.

name: Endothermic Dissolution of Ammonium Chloride in Water
explanation: Dissolving ammonium chloride in water absorbs lattice energy, causing a noticeable drop in solution temperature (cold pack principle).

name: Exothermic Dissolution of Calcium Chloride in Water
explanation: Dissolving anhydrous calcium chloride releases high hydration enthalpy, rapidly warming the solution (hot pack principle).

name: Reaction of Copper(II) Oxide with Sulfuric Acid
explanation: Gently warming black copper(II) oxide powder in dilute sulfuric acid dissolves the solid to form bright blue copper(II) sulfate solution.

verification.notes: Preparation of copper sulfate salt from insoluble oxide.

name: Reaction of Copper(II) Oxide with Hydrochloric Acid
explanation: Black copper oxide dissolves in warm hydrochloric acid forming aqueous copper(II) chloride with a distinctive blue-green color.

name: Crystallization of Copper(II) Sulfate Pentahydrate
explanation: Slow cooling or evaporation of saturated copper sulfate solution grows brilliant blue rhombic crystals of copper sulfate pentahydrate.

name: Electrolysis of Water
explanation: Passing electrical direct current through acidified water produces hydrogen gas at the cathode and oxygen gas at the anode in a 2:1 volume ratio.

name: Electrolysis of Aqueous Copper(II) Sulfate
explanation: Electrolyzing copper sulfate with inert carbon electrodes deposits shiny copper on the cathode while evolving oxygen gas bubbles at the anode.

verification.notes: Electroplating and electrolysis of copper sulfate.

name: Redox Reaction of Potassium Permanganate with Hydrogen Peroxide
explanation: Purple permanganate ions reduce to colorless Mn2+ ions while peroxide oxidizes to oxygen gas bubbles in acidic solution.

name: Redox Reaction between Iron(III) Chloride and Potassium Iodide
explanation: Fe3+ oxidizes iodide ions (I-) to elemental iodine (I2), causing the solution to turn dark reddish-brown.

name: Iodine-Starch Complex Formation
explanation: Triiodide ions slip inside amylose helix channels of starch to yield an extraordinarily dark blue-black inclusion complex.

name: Thermal Sublimation of Solid Iodine
explanation: Heating dark solid iodine crystals causes direct phase change into beautiful deep purple iodine gas vapor, which recrystallizes on cool glass surfaces.

verification.notes: Classic physical phase change / sublimation demonstration.
